messages.author: 899dbf724565c167
messages.subject: Habitat Suitability
parts:
Hi,

I was hoping for some clarity/suggestions with regards to habitat mask and habitat suitability.

I have finished analysing data from a camera trap survey within a fenced protected area (PA). I have run the SECR analysis with 3 different habitat masks. 1st with a hard fence boundary, 2nd with a uniform buffer of 12500m around the trap grid (permeable fence) and lastly a clipped 12500m buffer mask which had certain non-habitat areas removed outside the PA (variable fence permeability).

I was wondering if there is a means of including some sort of habitat suitability variable into the analysis which represents the expected lower habitat quality outside of the PA? I gather this kind of thing has been done my Royle et al. 2013 and Proffitt et al. 2015, using a Resource Selection Function (RSF), but is there a means of doing this in 'secr'? 

I should highlight I neither have telemetry data for RSF, nor does the camera trap grid extend outside of the PA.

Any comments or feedback would be greatly valued!

Best,
PJ

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Habitat Suitability
parts:
Hi
It is no problem in 'secr' to define a habitat (mask) covariate that takes different values/levels inside and outside the fence, and to use that in models for density. However I predict that your data will contain very little information on the relative densities, so densities both inside and outside will be estimated with large CI.
Murray
